findings.claim: `respell=False` covers only registration, so the frontmatter projections through `PUT /api/files/{id}/content` and the knowledge scanner's internal tag route still rename a shared Tag row to one note's case variant.
findings.impact: The registration fix now deliberately leaves notes whose frontmatter spelling differs from the row. Saving a body-only edit to such a note changes the chip on every other note that carries the tag, and the next chip edit on those notes writes the new spelling to disk. With the knowledge addon running, its projection of frontmatter tags should reach the same rename with no user action, which would undo what registration kept. In a deployment with that addon, r1's unattended respelling would then return one step later.
findings.evidence: backend/app/routers/files.py:1617 and backend/app/routers/internal.py:165 call `replace_file_tags` without `respell`, and the default at backend/app/services/tagops.py:50 is True. docs/ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md:531 says the internal route is used by the knowledge scanner to project frontmatter tags. decisions.md third run step 4 observed a PUT with a changed spelling rename the row and change the chips of a.md, b.md and c.md, while step 1 records b.md keeping `python` on disk against row `Python`. All R-5 runs record knowledge as absent. No test sends a body-only PUT for a note whose spelling differs from its row, or posts a case variant to the internal route and asserts another note's chip.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only reviewer; addon code is absent from this worktree). From reading: a.md has `tags: [Python]`; b.md with `tags: [python]` registers and joins row `Python`; PUT b.md's content with only its body changed; files.py:1617 passes `python` with respell=True, and tagops.py:78-82 renames the row, so a.md's chip reads `python`. Whether the knowledge scanner posts a new note's tags unchanged was not verified.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. The commit message keeps the rename for content PUTs on purpose, but it does not separate a save that leaves the tags alone from an intended rename, and the knowledge scanner route was not exercised.

findings.proposed_fix: Use `respell=False` on the internal route, and rename on a content PUT only when that note's frontmatter spelling changed from what its previous content said.

findings.claim: An upload or create over a missing row joins the row's own old case variant and keeps that spelling, even when no other note carries the tag.
findings.impact: Replacing a missing note that was the only carrier of `Alpha` with a note saying `alpha` shows chip `Alpha`, though no other note's chip needed protecting. The next chip edit silently rewrites the new file's frontmatter to `Alpha`, so the projection overrides the file that the rules call canonical.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/tagops.py:71-78 reads the index while the reused row still links its old tags, and with respell=False it keeps the folded match. The orphan sweep runs only afterwards at backend/app/services/upload.py:324 and backend/app/routers/drives.py:893. .claude/rules/design-decisions.md:62 makes frontmatter canonical for `.md`. decisions.md third run step 3 observed a chip add rewriting a note's disk spelling to the row's. TestReusedRow in backend/tests/test_frontmatter_tags_on_create.py uses `stale` against `Alpha, beta`, whose names do not fold together.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. From reading: seed a missing `n.md` whose only tag row is `Alpha`, carried by no other file, then upload `n.md` with `tags: [alpha]`. Expected from the code: chip `Alpha`, file on disk `alpha`, and after a chip add, file on disk `Alpha`.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. It is a side effect of the keep-as-it-stands rule on a case that rule's stated reason does not cover.

findings.proposed_fix: When a reused row's tags are replaced, release its old links and flush them before resolving names, or respell a row whose only carrier is this file.

findings.claim: Uploading a non-UTF-8 or over-limit `.md` over a reused row still skips projection with a bare `pass` or a false size guard, so the row keeps the old content's tags and logs nothing.
findings.impact: Chips and tag filter results describe content that no longer exists. Round r1's F5 is unchanged: the new non-UTF-8 test covers only a new row, which has no old tags to go stale.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/upload.py:321 is the size guard and upload.py:325-326 the silent `pass`, with the row reused at upload.py:278-301. backend/tests/test_frontmatter_tags_on_create.py `test_upload_of_non_utf8_note_succeeds_without_tags` starts with no row at that path. backend/app/routers/files.py:1620-1625 logs the equivalent PUT case. No test in the changed files uploads an over-limit note.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. From reading: a missing row n.md with tag `stale`, then an upload of n.md whose body has invalid UTF-8; the row is revived with `stale` attached. Mutation by reasoning: removing the size guard at upload.py:321 survives the changed test files.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. The input is uncommon for a notes tool, but the result is silently wrong in normal use.

findings.proposed_fix: Log the skip, and decide and test what a reused row whose new content cannot be read does with its old tags.

findings.claim: Copy still projects tags only up to 1,000,000 bytes while scan, upload and create accept up to 1,048,576 bytes, so a note in that gap loses its chips on copy.
findings.impact: A note between 1,000,001 and 1,048,576 bytes shows chips on the source and none on its copy, with no log line, and no later scan projects them because the row already exists. Rare, because it needs a note of nearly 1 MB. Round r1's F4 is unchanged.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/fileops.py:38 uses `1_000_000`; backend/app/services/scanner.py:284 and backend/app/services/upload.py:321 use `_MD_READ_MAX_BYTES`, and backend/app/routers/drives.py:885 allows 1 MiB on create. backend/app/services/fileops.py:334-336 skips the projection when the read returns None. No test covers the boundary.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. From reading: create a 1,020,000-byte `.md` with `tags: [a]`, then copy it; the source has chip `a` and the copy has none.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. The limit predates the change, and tag projection newly depends on it.

findings.proposed_fix: Use one shared limit constant for all Markdown projection reads.

specification_compliance: No invariants file or touch-point list exists for this change, and bucket A is unavailable. The only rule text judged against is .claude/rules/design-decisions.md:58-73 on tag editing.

r1 F1 and claude-read F2 (write-back failure skips tags) hold as fixed: scanner.py:294 now projects before the write-back at scanner.py:317, and `test_tags_survive_a_failed_id_writeback` covers both registration paths. decisions.md third run step 6 records it on a `:ro` mount.

r1 F2 and claude-read F1 (registration renames a shared row) hold as fixed for scan, single registration, upload, create and copy: all reach `project_frontmatter_tags`, which passes `respell=False` at tagops.py:104. The unattended rename remains on other projections (F1 here).

r1 F3 (swallowed flush poisons the session) holds as fixed for a flush inside the savepoint. A failure while `begin_nested` flushes earlier pending state before the savepoint exists is outside that isolation (see regression_risks).

r1 V1 (copy attaches a row pending delete) holds as fixed: `begin_nested` flushes the ghost's pending tag delete before the index is read, and `test_copy_onto_trashed_ghost_keeps_the_tag` depends on it. Both test session factories use autoflush=False like production, so the test is not masked by autoflush.

r1 F4 (copy limit) and r1 F5 / claude-read F3 (upload skip branch) are unchanged by the fix commits; see F4 and F3 here. r1 F6 (stale sidebar) is unfixed in code and is recorded in docs/developer-guide/known-issues.md.
design-decisions.md:69 (a projection failure must not undo a durable content write): every create and copy path tested keeps that for failures inside the savepoint.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Three spelling rules now exist for one row: registration joins it as it stands, a move joins it as it stands through its own loop in `retarget_file_tags`, and a content PUT or internal post renames it. Whether a body-only save counts as a tag edit is not declared anywhere found.

A chip can differ from its own note's frontmatter spelling for as long as the note is not chip-edited, and a chip edit then rewrites the note's spelling on disk (decisions.md third run steps 1 and 3). Which of the two a reader should treat as correct is not declared beyond frontmatter being canonical.

A CRLF note is read through `read_text` on scan, upload and copy, which normalises line endings, so its tags are projected. `PUT content` parses the raw body, where `parse` reports no frontmatter (frontmatter.py:110-112), and `_write_md_tags` answers 422 (frontmatter.py:155-158). A CRLF note keeping its line endings can therefore get chips at registration and lose them on a raw save. An id write-back during a scan rewrites the file with LF, so this needs a note that already has an id or sits on a read-only drive.

On a read-only drive the tags now project, while `md_id` and `md_aliases` still do not, because the OSError return at scanner.py:319-320 precedes both, so one note ends up with a partial projection and no log line.
regression_risks: Concurrency: `begin_nested` flushes the new row in `copy_file`, so the SQLite write lock is now held through `project_markdown_thumbnail` at fileops.py:337, which can produce a JPEG for a note with a local inline image. Before this change the row was not flushed until commit. Other writers wait for that time. No timing was measured.

Persistence: the `begin_nested` call is inside the `try` at tagops.py:95-99. A failure flushing earlier pending state, such as the copy's own INSERT, is logged as a tags projection failure with no exception detail, and the session then needs a rollback. On copy the next query raises and the existing handler reverses the file with a 500, so it stays loud, but the log line names the wrong cause. On the create path over a missing row, `cleanup_orphan_tags` would surface it outside any handler after the file was replaced on disk.

Persistence: the engine in database.py:15-27 does not take over pysqlite's transaction control, so a SAVEPOINT with no earlier write on the connection is the outermost one and its RELEASE commits. Each path normally writes first. The exception found is an upload over an active row where no column changes, and the commit there follows almost immediately, so the only loss is atomicity with the sweep. Reasoned, not run.
Persistence: the warning at tagops.py:107 has no `exc_info`, unlike the equivalent paths at files.py:1626-1630, so a real projection failure cannot be diagnosed from the log.
Scope: a scan of many new notes loads the drive's Tag rows once per note with frontmatter (tagops.py:71) and opens one savepoint per note. Cost was not measured.
Submodules: `app.routers.files.replace_file_tags` remains importable through files.py:92, and internal.py:26 uses it. No test in backend/tests patches that name. The diff contains no gitlink change.
test_coverage: Mutations reasoned, not run. Removing `begin_nested` should fail `test_failing_flush_leaves_session_usable` and `test_copy_onto_trashed_ghost_keeps_the_tag`. Passing `respell=True` should fail both `..._joins_..._as_it_stands` tests. Moving the projection after the write-back should fail `test_tags_survive_a_failed_id_writeback`. Narrowing the upload except clause should fail `test_upload_of_non_utf8_note_succeeds_without_tags`.
Case-variant joining is tested for scan, single registration and cross-drive copy. Upload and create share the helper but have no case-variant test.
The failing flush is tested only for scan and single registration. Upload, create and copy have no such test, and a failing flush before the savepoint has none anywhere.
Not covered: a body-only PUT of a note whose spelling differs from its row, or a case-variant post to the internal route, asserting another note's chip (F1).
Not covered: a reused row whose new tag folds onto its own old row (F2); an over-limit upload or a non-UTF-8 upload over a reused row (F3); the copy size boundary (F4).
`test_cross_drive_joins_destination_row_as_it_stands` now seeds rows on both drives and asserts the destination row id, which closes claude-read F4's drive-scoping gap for cross-drive copy.
not_verified: No test, mutation or application run was performed, because this reviewer has read-only tools. Every repro is reasoned from code or quoted from decisions.md.
SQLAlchemy and pysqlite behaviour was read from memory and not observed: savepoint rollback expiry, a failed flush at `begin_nested` entry, and RELEASE of an outermost savepoint.
Addon code under addons/ is absent from this worktree, so what the knowledge scanner posts, when, and for which notes was not read. That part of F1 rests on docs/ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md:531.
The JPEG work inside `project_markdown_thumbnail` was read only as far as markdown_images.py:395, and its duration under the write lock was not measured.
The frontend's `saveFileTags` and editor line-ending behaviour were not read, so how a CRLF note behaves through the UI is unconfirmed.
R-5 observations in decisions.md were not independently repeated. Files were read from the working tree and assumed to match commit db7aa7e74.
trajectory: Of the fix commits, 933ca488b and db7aa7e74 add only review records and change no code. c6c022417 is the one code round: it adds a `respell` mode to `replace_file_tags` (a new branch) and a savepoint with a stated prediction about what it flushes and confines (a new state), and it moves the scanner call without adding to it. With a single code round there is no repeated pattern across rounds of the same branch or state being added again, so the record does not yet show the design being patched. The new mode does create a warning sign: the spelling decision now differs per caller and is scoped by a flag, and F1 and F2 are cases that flag does not settle, so a further fix there that adds another flag or caller condition would be patching. No round removed a branch or state.

perspectives.notes: The savepoint flush now takes the write lock before the index is read on every path, which closes r1's copy window between index read and lock. The new cost is the lock held across thumbnail work in copy, recorded under regression risks. No silent wrong result from concurrency was found.
